dunning.title: Dunning
dunning.subtitle: Chase overdue invoices with escalating reminders.

dunning.noOverdue: No overdue invoices: there is nothing to chase.
dunning.alreadyProposed: The dunning run for this date already exists: it is shown below.
dunning.nothingToIssue: Every proposed invoice has been paid in the meantime: nothing to issue.

empty.title: No dunning runs yet
empty.hint: A dunning run reads the overdue invoices from the open items list and proposes the next reminder level per invoice.

permissionDenied.read: You lack the permission to read the dunning area.

config.title: Settings
config.hint: The three reminder levels are a business convention, not a legal deadline. All three save together.
config.intervalHint: The minimum interval keeps the reminders apart: a later level is reached only once that many days have passed since the previous reminder was issued, so an invoice that is already long overdue still escalates one letter at a time rather than all at once. The default is 10 days.
config.feeHint: A reminder fee has no statutory basis: it is only chargeable when contractually agreed and reasonable. A charged fee always books, and its VAT automatically follows the chased invoice's own rates.
config.interestHint: Default interest is 5% per year by law (Art. 104 OR); only a higher contractual rate is allowed. It is computed on the open invoice amount (actual days, 365-day year), shown on the letter, and never booked.

error.interestFloor: The interest rate is below the statutory 5% (Art. 104 OR).
error.needsAccount: A booked fee needs an income account.
error.invalid: The settings are incomplete: check the levels.

Dunning.title: Dunning
Dunning.body: Dunning works in runs: propose collects the overdue open items, you review the run, then issue and send. Levels, deadlines, fees and default interest come from your dunning policy; every figure in the run is frozen and traceable. Issuing and sending are separate, deliberate steps.
